speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, I will explain why the choice of words "US-China" and "trade conflict" is not exactly very precise.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For the second part, I will answer what we need to do as a country and as companies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, the challenges that we are facing in the external environment are not exactly limited to only the tensions between the United States (US) and China.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The uncertainties around the world have gone beyond the US and China.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They include the uncertainties with Brexit, Japan and Korea, Hong Kong and others.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It has also affected the functioning of the World Trade Organization system, of which the challenges to the continued functioning of the appellate body are a serious concern for all of us.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, it is not just about the US and China.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The second part is that it is also not just about the trade war.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The competition between the US and China today has gone beyond trade to encompass technology and other issues.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, it is a more multifaceted challenge that we are dealing with.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: With that as the backdrop, the question is: how do we, as a country and as companies, adapt and adjust our strategies amidst all these uncertainties?

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The second part of diversification has to do with supply chains.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In this world of flux, supply chains might be disrupted because of economic and political reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is why the economic agencies are working closely with all our companies to make sure that our sources of materials, labour and other factors of production will continuously stay robust and resilient amidst these shifting geopolitical tensions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Last but not least, we must continue to diversify our product mix as an economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must make sure that no one particular sector dominates the economy to the extent that it causes us to be much more fragile than we need be.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, that diversification of our economy and product mix actually helps us to stabilise the overall economic performance.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The second strategy that we need to adopt amidst all this flux is to make sure that we continue to innovate and invest.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, we must make sure that we continuously do better to translate our research outcomes into enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must complete the research, innovation and enterprise cycle – not a chain, but a cycle.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must build real capabilities beyond building capacities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must compete on the basis of real capabilities, rather than just capacities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For countries that are much bigger than us, with much stronger and a more diverse resource base, they might compete on the basis of capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But for us, we compete on the basis of capability.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is often said that many countries are competing on the low-mix, high-volume products.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: That is a lot to do with capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For us, if we are to be serious in competing with what we call the high-mix, low-volume products, then, research and innovation, intellectual property protection, and quality standards are all very important, and those play to our strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The second thing that we need to invest much more in is the adoption and proliferation of our digital platforms, especially amongst the small and medium enterprises (SMEs) within our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They are available in the market and we are committed to working with our Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) to make sure that we accelerate the pace of adoption.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When we achieve critical mass, it will also bring about a virtuous cycle for us to reduce the price of adoption and allow businesses to do business with one another more easily.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Last but not least, with or without the current challenges amidst the global uncertainties, we must continuously look at our production system and processes.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There is always room for us to innovate in such things, beyond the innovation of products.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is about the innovation in production systems and processes that can make us more productive.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The third prong of the strategy has to do with training.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There are three subparts to the training strategy which we need to focus on.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have often talked about the training of workers and that is well-known.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will continue to invest heavily in the training of our workers, especially in the acquisition of skills for the Industry 4.0 journey, digital platforms and so forth.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is an area where SkillsFuture Singapore, Workforce Singapore, the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and the TACs must work closely to bring the level of the skills of our workers up to speed with what is required by the markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Having said that, it is necessary but insufficient just to focus only on workers' training.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We also need to focus more heavily on the training of the leadership teams in the respective companies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is an area that I have discussed with the many TACs and we can do much more.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: From my own experience in NTUC, before we even talk about the training of the workers, it is most important for us to open up the vision of the management team.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Last but not least, when it comes to training, we will have to do much more to better organise ourselves and our respective agencies, from the TACs to the overseas missions from the Economic Development Board, Enterprise Singapore and other economic agencies, so that we can combine the market knowledge that we have to help our enterprises to diversify their markets beyond Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, Mr Speaker, Sir, in short, the current situation warrants us to take a close look at how we develop our companies and economies, and we must go beyond looking at just the US-China issues or looking at it as just a trade issue.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There are various things that we must do, regardless of whether it is US-China or whether it is a trade issue.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Continue to diversify our markets, continue to diversify our supply chains and product mix.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And focus on sharing market knowledge with all our available agencies.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The first is, will we see more regional trade pacts to overcome any side effects of the US-China trade standoff and Brexit which the Minister alluded to in his response?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And innovation being capability-focused, rather than capacity-focused, which was what the Minister alluded to in his reply.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will continue to expand our network of FTAs, both in terms of numbers and also in terms of the quality.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But more important than that, beyond reducing the tariffs associated with the trade negotiations, we must increasingly focus on the lowering of what we call "non-tariff barriers".

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because sometimes, the gains from lowering tariff barriers could be eroded by the imposition of new non-tariff barriers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is a challenge, not just for the region, but also worldwide.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These include the standards for healthcare products, the standards for food, the standards of mutual recognition and so on.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is what we mean by non-tariff barriers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, that is under negotiation at this point in time.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the Member's second question, yes, there are two parts to the regional innovation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), we have a very lively startup community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, I am very happy when I meet the young startup entrepreneurs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They no longer see their role as serving only one particular market.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, most of the time, they see themselves as what they call an "ASEAN company".

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They started their operations with a vision to serve the entire region.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There is a very lively startup scene in ASEAN, particularly in Singapore, Indonesia and Vietnam.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, beyond the startup scene, it is also very important for us to enable the multinational corporations (MNCs) to innovate and develop their products across different markets to serve the region.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These MNCs can be from within the region or from beyond the region.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Regardless, our challenge is to make sure that we have the enabling environment, the business rules that allow them to innovate across borders and to make use of the talent from different parts of the region to come together to develop those new products and services to serve the market.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Minister spoke about innovation capability among Singapore-based enterprises.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the Minister satisfied with the current trend or direction of innovation capability among Singapore enterprises?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: No Ministry, no agency, no country will ever say that they are happy with what they have.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, the more important question is, how can we do better?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The biggest challenge for any research, innovation and enterprise cycle is this: how do we translate research into innovation and enterprise?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Essentially, as Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean would say – how do you translate money into research outcome and translate research outcome back into money?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is always very difficult to find in one person a scientist, an innovator and an entrepreneur.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The challenge and the lesson we have learnt from other countries is to make sure that, while these may not all reside within one person, we must have an environment where both the entrepreneurs and the scientists are able to constantly mix with one another to generate those ideas for both businesses and for scientific research.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is this combination that is most important in any scientific community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When I was studying in the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, they have been able to achieve this ecosystem very well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Within every class that you go to in business school, there are the scientists, the researchers, there are also the people who have a very keen sense of business to know what is possible.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is this mix that many places around the world are trying to emulate because that is how we can percolate the ideas and bring research outcomes into market opportunities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, this is one area that everyone wants to do better in.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second area that we will always strive to do better is to make sure that the funding ecosystem provides that continuum of funding options for new enterprises from the startup stage, all the way through until they perhaps one day get listed on the market.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That chain is also something that, across the entire globe, everyone is working very hard to make sure that new enterprises have those options to bring their business ideas to fruition.
